name: Carbonate / bicarbonate equilibrium (acid-base speciation; pH + charge)

provenance.ref: Aquatic Chemistry: carbonate system pK1=6.35, pK2=10.33 (freshwater, 25C)

notes: Diversity-first stress component #4: the acid/base + pH probe. It surfaced a real schema finding: the neutral-formula-as-identity convention (from component #2, for pyruvate) BREAKS here -- bicarbonate (HCO3-, 1 H) and carbonate (CO3--, 0 H) both neutralize to H2CO3 (2 H), which would collapse distinct species and miscount hydrogen. RESOLUTION: formula carries the species' ACTUAL protonation (atoms), entity_id (ChEBI) is the identity that distinguishes HCO3- from CO3--, and CHARGE is a first-class facet so the acid/base reactions are charge-balance verified, not only mass. RATE CONSTANTS ARE REAL: the forward/reverse ratios reproduce the measured equilibrium constants -- kf1/kr1 = Ka1 = 10^-6.35 M (= 4.467e-4 in mM at V=1), kf2/kr2 = Ka2 = 10^-10.33 M (= 4.677e-8 in mM); reverse rates are a nominal relaxation timescale. So the equilibrium speciation and the resulting pH (~4.2 for CO2-saturated water) are physically real, not fabricated. This box is CLOSED and atom+charge balanced by construction.

validity.note: mass-action relaxation to carbonate equilibrium; illustrative rate constants. Aqueous, dilute.
